A1.justification: Both complete, readable 47-page PDFs describe HarDBench and SUBA, including Appendices A and B. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons establish that only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and its link differ.

before.justification: v1 reports original jailbreak evaluations, SUBA safety and utility experiments, human validation, and supplementary analyses in Sections 5–6 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experimental results, human validation, and supplementary analyses in Sections 5–6 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: The draft-generation pipeline, co-authoring prompts, preference labeling, and SUBA procedures using KTO and GRPO are identical, including Appendix A.5's reward formulation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four harmful domains, eight benign domains, four utility benchmarks, and Paraphrased HQ evaluation scenario. Appendix B's keyword lists are identical.

E2.justification: Tables 4 and 9 retain identical participation by Zero-shot, Safety Prompt, HQ-trained SUBA, and SUBA without benign data. No comparator is added, removed, or revised.

E3.justification: The 100-per-domain test sampling, prompting conditions, model configurations, HS/ASR/RAR metrics, human-evaluation protocols, and KTO/GRPO training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: Task-framing and training-data ablations, paraphrased-query robustness, evaluator validation, domain analyses, and benign and harmful case studies are identical in the main text and Appendix A.

E5.justification: Fixed-seed sampling and the human-agreement and correlation reporting in Tables 5, 8, 11, and 12 are unchanged. There is no addition or revision of repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–12 and findings in the figures match. For example, GPT-4o's CoJP ASR remains 96.75% in Table 1, and LLaMA3-8B SUBA using KTO remains at 5.25% in Tables 4 and 9.

T1.justification: Metric definitions, the binary GRPO reward formulation, and benchmark score transformations in Appendices A.5 and A.8 are identical. No formal assumption, theorem, proof, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion make identical claims about draft-based co-authoring vulnerability, HarDBench, and SUBA's safety–utility balance.

C2.justification: The task-framing explanations, safety–utility interpretations, actionable-specificity discussion, and limitations concerning alignment methods, domain coverage, and fixed prompt templates are unchanged.

D1.justification: Prompt templates, generation and labeling instructions, GPU hardware, LoRA settings, and optimization hyperparameters are identical. The benchmark repository link and stated controlled-access policy also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the complete reference list are identical, as is the positioning relative to existing jailbreak benchmarks, disguise-based attacks, and preference optimization research.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, dated 21 Apr 2026, to v2, dated 9 Jun 2026, with its associated link updated. Manuscript wording, title, authors, terminology, and section organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–21, Tables 1–12, captions, formatting, and placement are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–47 are identical; the only visual difference on page 1 is the updated marginal version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: v2 updates only the arXiv version/date stamp and its link. The scientific content, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and presentation throughout the main text and appendices are otherwise identical, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
